LESSON: HOUSES FOUND AT HOME • TOILET • LATRINE • KITCHEN • POULTRY • GRANARY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Home
Topic 3.1: Houses found at home • Toilet • Latrine • Kitchen • Poultry • Granary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Houses found at home • Toilet • Latrine • Kitchen • Poultry • Granary, part of Our Home in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have houses at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Houses found at home • Toilet • Latrine • Kitchen • Poultry • Granary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: as learner models houses in a home and relates them to their uses.

Values:
Unity: as learner collaborates with peers to model a simple house found at home using clay or plasticine.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental education: learner enhances environmental awareness as they identify houses found at home.

Social cohesion: learner collaboratively models different types of houses at home.

Link to other learning areas :

Drawn pictures of houses found at home relates to pattern making in Creative Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts, picture cards , flash cards, braille cards, glue, crayons, coloured pencil, photos, sticks, paints, maize cobs, grass, video clips, clay,

models, tactile diagrams.
